- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3+ in 3-5 days), model often overcorrects downward; delay or dampen the correction to allow for mean reversion.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.2) and prices are falling, model often underestimates the drop; increase forecast downward to reflect stronger bearish momentum.
- Model frequently underestimates true price peaks in the 10-15 day horizon; adjust upward slightly for medium-term forecasts if sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile (±0.3–0.6), model tends to smooth out extremes; introduce slight asymmetry to reflect sentiment-driven volatility.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture late-period sentiment shifts; anchor final 5–7 days to sentiment history if sentiment turns sharply.
- If recent sentiment is consistently high (e.g., 1.0 for 3+ days), model may overfit to recent highs; apply a 10–15% downward bias to prevent overconfidence.
